renderToString.summary: Renders a component to HTML on the server, its shadow root written as a declarative shadow root, which the browser shows before any script runs.
renderToString.description:
The component runs as in the browser up to its render: it is constructed, the given inputs are set by assigning their properties, as code outside Xaendar sets them, then onInit runs and the template is rendered, each signal read once. The components it renders are rendered the same way. The promise resolves to the HTML of the element of the component: its tag, with the attributes and the classes its @HostProperty declare, a <template shadowrootmode="open"> holding its stylesheet, in a <style>, and its template, then its end tag. A script after the element, the event contract, records what the user does until the runtime is there, which replays it.

The server writes HTML once, so what reacts or listens in the browser does not run: the effects of this.effect(), afterRender and onDestroy, the listeners of the events and of @HostEvent, the host directives and the custom directives of a component, and the queries, which keep their initial value. The custom directives of a native element are applied: each one is constructed, its properties are set, its onInit runs and its @HostProperty are written on the element, while its effects, its events and onDestroy do not run. The content it assigns to this.element.innerHTML is written as the content of the element, so a directive filling its element can write it in onInit on the server only (typeof window === 'undefined'), its effect writing it in the browser. A component created with createComponent is constructed, not rendered. The structural directives run, since they decide what is rendered, and the promise of an asynchronous one is awaited: a rejected one renders nothing.

An expression of a template reads the globals of the browser through globalThis: on the server, one Node lacks, such as window, is undefined, instead of throwing a ReferenceError. An element ref is undefined on the server. A custom element whose class the server does not define, such as one imported with @import lazy, is written without shadow root: the browser renders it once its class is defined.

Comments mark the dynamic parts of the HTML for the browser: the interpolations, the blocks of @if, @switch and @for, with the items of the latter, and the elements structural directives are applied to. The inputs are written as JSON into the data-xd-inputs attribute of the element, which the browser sets them from before the component renders, and the transfer state of options into a <script type="application/json" data-xd-state> following it.

The server DOM must be installed with loadServerDom() before the modules of @xaendar/core and of the components are evaluated, and the components must be built for the server by the Vite plugin, with its ssr option.

members.component: The class of the component, decorated with @WebComponent: the selector it is defined with is the tag of the HTML.
members.inputs: The inputs to set, each one with its value, by the name of its property, not by its alias, as createComponent binds them, with values in place of getters. Each value goes through the transform of its input. Defaults to none: every input keeps its default value. See RenderInputs. A required input left out throws.
members.options: The transfer state of the page: see RenderOptions. Defaults to none.

entry.title: In the entry of the server
entry.body: The entry installs the Signal polyfill and the server DOM first, then loads @xaendar/ssr and the components on demand, and exports the function the server calls for each page. xd new --ssr generates it.

output.title: What it returns
output.body: The element of the component, with its host attributes and its declarative shadow root, and, inside it, the components it renders, each one with its own. The HTML is a single line: here it is split for reading.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: The promise is rejected when the component is not defined, when it has no template compiled for the server, when an input or a value of the transfer state cannot be written into the HTML, such as a function, and when the code of a component throws while it is rendered, such as a constructor reading document. The server of the application generated by xd new --ssr then sends the root component without content, which the browser renders. See the Error encyclopedia.

RenderInputs.summary: The type of the inputs renderToString sets on the component it renders.
RenderInputs.description: An object with an optional property for each input of the component, named like the property declaring it with @Property, holding its value: the inputs createComponent binds, with values in place of getters. A member that is not an input is not a property of it.

typing.title: Checking the inputs
typing.body: TypeScript checks the names and the values against the inputs of the class: a misspelled name, or a value of another type, fails the type check.

RenderOptions.summary: The options of renderToString: the transfer state of the page and the nonce of the response.
RenderOptions.description: The third argument of renderToString(). The transfer state carries the data the entry fetched to render the page, so that the browser starts from them without fetching them again. The nonce lets the event contract run under a strict Content-Security-Policy.

members.nonce: The nonce of the Content-Security-Policy of the response, written on the script of the event contract, which a strict policy would block as any inline script. It must be a new one for each response, the same of the header. Defaults to none.
members.state: A value for each key, written as JSON into a <script type="application/json" data-xd-state> following the element of the component. The components read a value with getTransferState(key), on the server while the page is rendered and in the browser from the page. The JSON carries undefined, NaN, ±Infinity, a bigint, a Date, a Map and a Set too; a function, an instance of another class or an object containing itself rejects the promise. Defaults to none: nothing is written.
